correctness.rationale: For nonnegative real virtual budget B with unit cost, fixed candidate priority, and sunflower approval ballots C∪P_j (disjoint petals), core purchases always have price 1/n, below the private price 1/n_j when there are at least two ballot types. Once u=|C| core projects are purchased, supporter groups decouple and group j funds exactly min(|P_j|,floor(n_j(B-u)/n)) projects in priority order. For B<u the outcome is C^[floor B]. This reconstructs all quantifiers, ties, no-completion rule, and integer threshold boundaries. Two arbitrary distinct ballots always decompose into such a sunflower. For voters {A,B},{A,B,D},{C,D}, exact balance/price calculations give W(3)={A,B,C} and W(4)={A,B,D}: after buying A,B at B=4, D costs price 2/3 versus C's price 1. Hence the minimum number of voters exhibiting nonnesting is three.

originality.rationale: Peters–Skowron's laminar proportionality addresses fixed-size/integral party-list proportionality; the claim gives a path simultaneously for all real budgets and makes private entry thresholds explicit. Lackner–Skowron's book already supplies a four-voter MES monotonicity counterexample, not a three-voter minimum. Kraiczy–Elkind studies a distinct adaptive MES and the motivation of budget changes, not this uncompleted MES parametric theorem.
residual_risks: Equivalent all-budget sunflower path or three-voter witness may occur in specialized MES notes, discussion appendices, or unindexed manuscripts.
Applies only to uncompleted unit-cost approval MES and one fixed cross-budget tie priority; no claims for completed MES, variable costs, or changing tie priority.

value.rationale: Budget sensitivity of the uncompleted Method of Equal Shares is a motivated question because virtual budgets are varied repeatedly in participatory-budget allocation. The theorem provides exact entry events for arbitrarily many voter groups and projects, with nonintegral quotas, rather than only an existence guarantee at a fixed committee size. The three-voter example establishes the sharp structural boundary by number of voters.
